title: The Fed Has Two Tools to Influence Money Market Conditions

source.name: NY Fed Liberty Street Economics RSS

summary: NY Fed staff researchers Adam Copeland and Owen Engbretson analyze how two Fed monetary policy tools—administrative rates (IORB) and balance sheet size (Fed liabilities)—affect money market conditions using confidential trade-level Treasury repo data from OFR. Their empirical estimates show both tools significantly influence the liquidity risk premium that dealers charge to intermediate funding, with IORB increases and Fed liability decreases driving up spreads. The average dealer spread to intermediate funding was 7.5 basis points during the 2020-2024 sample period.
key_points: Analysis uses Treasury repo data from OFR's centrally cleared repo collection capturing most interdealer trading and dealer-to-client trades via the Sponsored Service program
IORB increased from 15 to 540 basis points from early 2020 to end of 2024, with three decreases in the last half of 2024
Fed liabilities (reserves plus overnight reverse repo facility) peaked at nearly $6 trillion in 2021 and fell to $3.5 trillion by December 2024
A one standard deviation increase in IORB (226 bps) drives up the liquidity risk premium by 2.1 to 3.5 basis points
A one standard deviation increase in Fed liabilities ($750 billion) drives down the liquidity risk premium by 1.6 to 2.5 basis points
The estimated effect of balance sheet changes on the liquidity risk premium is larger when IORB is low compared to when IORB is high (nonlinear effects)
why_it_matters: Understanding how the Fed's dual tools affect money market spreads is critical for market participants and policymakers. The research demonstrates that the Fed can decouple economic policy goals from financing conditions—for example, lowering rates to support the economy while shrinking the balance sheet to maintain tighter money market conditions. This has direct implications for how the Fed manages the transition from abundant to ample reserves and for monitoring systemic risks in secured funding markets.
market_structure_context: This research directly addresses market plumbing by quantifying how Fed tools affect dealer intermediation spreads in the Treasury repo market. Dealers intermediate between cash-rich investors (money market mutual funds) and levered clients (hedge funds), and the liquidity risk premium they charge reflects the opportunity cost of holding liquid securities buffers. The $5+ trillion repo market is the dominant secured funding market in the U.S. The research identifies nonlinear interactions between IORB and balance sheet tools, with balance sheet effects being larger when rates are lower.
notes: Source is recent (published 6 days before TODAY), high-quality NY Fed staff research using confidential trade-level data. Article is a blog post summarizing a Staff Report. The body was truncated at the end but the key empirical findings and takeaways are captured. Article provides concrete quantitative estimates that are directly useful for understanding Fed tool transmission to money markets.
